docs.title: H2S Corrosion Prediction
docs.text: NACE-compliant sour service corrosion rate prediction and remaining life assessment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "H2S Corrosion Prediction", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Source: Synthetic data generator (CorrosionDataGenerator)
  • Samples: 3,000 corrosion records
  • Parameters: H2S concentration, CO2 concentration, temperature, pressure, pH, flow velocity, pipe material
  • Targets: corrosion_rate_mpy (regression), remaining_useful_life_years (regression)

docs.title: Corrosion Rate Predictor
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoostingRegressor
  • Task: Predict corrosion rate in mils per year (mpy)
  • Input: 7 features (6 numeric + 1 categorical)
  • Output: Corrosion rate (mpy)
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Remaining Useful Life Estimator
docs.text:
• Algorithm: RandomForestRegressor
  • Task: Predict remaining useful life in years
  • Input: Same 7 features as predictor
  • Output: Remaining life (years)
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline
docs.text:
• ColumnTransformer with:
  • StandardScaler for 6 numeric features
  • OneHotEncoder for pipe_material (3 categories)
  • Pipeline object saved as pipeline.pkl for consistent transforms at inference

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask
  • Port: 5010
  • Format: JSON request/response
  • Endpoints: 5 (predict, life, health, models, docs)

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JS (Jinja2 templates)
  • Theme: Dark theme UI

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Input -> JSON with 7 corrosion parameters
  2. Transform -> ColumnTransformer applies scaling + encoding
  3. Predict -> GradientBoosting (rate) or RandomForest (life)
  4. Output -> JSON with prediction and status

docs.title: Feature Processing
docs.text: Feature Transform Description h2s_concentration_ppm StandardScaler H2S concentration co2_concentration_pct StandardScaler CO2 concentration temperature_c StandardScaler Temperature pressure_mpa StandardScaler Pressure ph StandardScaler Fluid pH flow_velocity_ms StandardScaler Flow velocity pipe_material OneHotEncoder Pipe material (3 categories)

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.9-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN python train.py

EXPOSE 5010

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
docker build -t h2s-corrosion-prediction .
docker run -p 5010:5010 h2s-corrosion-prediction

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  h2s-corrosion-prediction:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5010:5010"
    environment:
      - FLASK_ENV=production
    volumes:
      - model-data:/app/outputs

volumes:
  model-data:

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default FLASK_ENV Flask environment mode development PORT Server port 5010

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn for production serving: bash gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:5010 app:app
  • Set debug=False in app.py (set to True by default - change for production)
  • Configure reverse proxy (nginx) for SSL termination
  • Set up health check monitoring on /api/health
  • Use a process manager (systemd, supervisor) for auto-restart

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
1. python train.py generates synthetic data and trains models
  2. Models + preprocessing pipeline saved to outputs/models/
  3. python app.py loads models and starts the API server

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml): - Runs on push to main - Installs dependencies - Runs training pipeline - Executes API tests

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The H2S Corrosion Prediction System uses machine learning to predict hydrogen sulfide (H2S) induced corrosion rates and estimate remaining useful life for oil and gas pipelines.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd h2s-corrosion-prediction
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

This generates 3,000 synthetic corrosion samples and trains: - Corrosion Rate Predictor (GradientBoostingRegressor) - Remaining Useful Life Estimator (RandomForestRegressor)

docs.title: Run the Server
docs.text:
python app.py

Open http://localhost:5010 in your browser.

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Corrosion Rate Panel - Predict pipe corrosion rate (mpy) from environmental conditions
  • Remaining Life Panel - Estimate pipeline remaining useful life (years)
  • Model Information - View loaded models and their types
  • Dark Theme UI - Modern dark-themed dashboard

docs.title: Predict Corrosion Rate (curl)
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5010/api/predict \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "h2s_concentration_ppm": 500,
    "co2_concentration_pct": 3.5,
    "temperature_c": 80,
    "pressure_mpa": 10.0,
    "ph": 5.5,
    "flow_velocity_ms": 3.0,
    "pipe_material": "carbon_steel"
  }'

docs.text:
import requests

response = requests.post("http://localhost:5010/api/predict", json={
    "h2s_concentration_ppm": 500,
    "co2_concentration_pct": 3.5,
    "temperature_c": 80,
    "pressure_mpa": 10.0,
    "ph": 5.5,
    "flow_velocity_ms": 3.0,
    "pipe_material": "carbon_steel"
})

print(f"Corrosion rate: {result['corrosion_rate_mpy']} mpy")

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
1. Gather operating conditions (H2S/CO2 levels, temperature, pressure, pH, velocity, material)
  2. Call /api/predict to get the corrosion rate
  3. Call /api/life to estimate remaining useful life
  4. Plan maintenance based on results

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Models not loaded: Run python train.py first
  • Input error: Ensure all 7 fields are provided with valid ranges
  • Pipe material: Must be exactly carbon_steel, stainless_steel, or coated

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
